title: Atari Releases Pong
shortDesc: A simple two-paddle tennis game becomes the first big arcade hit.
fullDesc: In 1972 Atari released Pong, a simple electronic table tennis game made by Nolan Bushnell and Al Alcorn. Its arcade cabinets earned far more than expected and launched the video game industry.
realFacts: Atari was founded in 1972 by Nolan Bushnell and Ted Dabney
Home Pong arrived in 1975
Warner Communications bought Atari in 1976
The Atari 2600 console followed in 1977

title: Space Invaders Takes Over the Arcades
shortDesc: Taito's alien shooter turns video games into a worldwide craze.
fullDesc: Taito released Space Invaders in Japan in 1978, designed by Tomohiro Nishikado. Players shot rows of descending aliens, and the game became a global arcade phenomenon.
realFacts: Hundreds of thousands of arcade cabinets were sold
The Atari 2600 version in 1980 boosted console sales
It helped create the idea of the high score
It influenced shooters for decades

title: Pac-Man Is Released
shortDesc: A yellow circle eating dots becomes the most famous video game character.
fullDesc: Namco released Pac-Man in Japan in 1980, designed by Toru Iwatani, and it reached the United States later that year. Its maze chase and cute ghosts appealed to a wide audience beyond typical arcade players.
realFacts: Each ghost has its own chasing behaviour
Ms. Pac-Man followed in 1982
A perfect game scores 3,333,360 points
It became one of the highest-grossing arcade games ever

title: Tetris Is Created in Moscow
shortDesc: A Soviet programmer's falling-blocks puzzle becomes one of the best-selling games ever.
fullDesc: In 1984 Alexey Pajitnov, working at the Soviet Academy of Sciences in Moscow, created Tetris. After a tangled licensing fight, it shipped with the Game Boy in 1989 and sold hundreds of millions of copies across versions.
realFacts: Nintendo bundled Tetris with the Game Boy in 1989
Henk Rogers helped secure the rights from the Soviet Union
Pajitnov moved to the United States in 1996
More than 500 million copies have been sold across versions

title: Super Mario Bros. Launches
shortDesc: Nintendo's platformer helps revive the video game industry.
fullDesc: Nintendo released Super Mario Bros. in 1985 for the Nintendo Entertainment System, designed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka. Its smooth controls and level design set the standard for platform games.
realFacts: It sold more than 40 million copies
The NES helped rebuild the industry after the 1983 crash
Koji Kondo wrote its famous theme music
Mario became one of the best-known characters in the world

title: The Legend of Zelda Debuts
shortDesc: An open adventure game that lets players explore freely and save their progress.
fullDesc: Nintendo released The Legend of Zelda in Japan in 1986, created by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka. It let players explore a large world in any order and was one of the first console games to save progress on the cartridge.
realFacts: The NES version in 1987 used a battery to save progress
The series has produced dozens of games
Breath of the Wild in 2017 reimagined its open world
Miyamoto based it on exploring the countryside as a child

title: Sonic the Hedgehog Races In
shortDesc: Sega introduces a fast blue mascot to take on Mario.
fullDesc: Sega released Sonic the Hedgehog in 1991 for the Genesis, created by Yuji Naka, Naoto Ohshima and Hirokazu Yasuhara. Its speed and attitude gave Sega a mascot to compete with Nintendo's Mario.
realFacts: It was a pack-in game with the Genesis
Sega gained a large share of the US market in the early 1990s
Many sequels and spin-offs followed
Sonic later appeared in films and television

title: Doom Is Released
shortDesc: A shareware shooter defines first-person gaming and PC modding.
fullDesc: id Software released Doom on December 10, 1993, led by John Carmack and John Romero. Its fast 3D action, network multiplayer and easy modding made it a landmark of PC gaming.
realFacts: The first episode was shared free as shareware
It popularised online deathmatch
Players made huge numbers of custom levels
It sparked public debate about violence in games

title: Pokémon Debuts in Japan
shortDesc: Two Game Boy games begin the best-selling media franchise in history.
fullDesc: Pokémon Red and Green launched in Japan on February 27, 1996, created by Satoshi Tajiri's Game Freak. The games spread worldwide in 1998 and grew into trading cards, a TV show and films.
realFacts: Red and Blue reached the West in 1998
The trading card game launched in 1996
Pokémon became a huge worldwide franchise
Pokémon Go in 2016 brought it to smartphones

title: Half-Life Changes Shooters
shortDesc: Valve's first game tells its story without leaving the player's eyes.
fullDesc: Valve released Half-Life in November 1998. It told its story through scripted events in the first-person view instead of cutscenes, and it became one of the most praised shooters ever made.
realFacts: It was Valve's first game
Counter-Strike began as a Half-Life mod
Valve created Steam in 2003 partly to update its games
Half-Life 2 followed in 2004

title: Steam Launches
shortDesc: Valve's software platform turns PC games into digital downloads.
fullDesc: Valve launched Steam in September 2003, first as a way to update its own games. It grew into the largest digital store for PC games and changed how people buy and play them.
realFacts: Half-Life 2 required Steam in 2004
Third-party games joined from 2005
Tens of millions of people use it at the same time
Seasonal sales became a PC gaming tradition

title: World of Warcraft Launches
shortDesc: Blizzard's online world draws millions of subscribers.
fullDesc: Blizzard launched World of Warcraft on November 23, 2004. The massively multiplayer online game grew to more than ten million subscribers at its peak and set the model for online role-playing games.
realFacts: It peaked at around 12 million subscribers in 2010
Expansions have been released regularly since 2007
It popularised subscription online gaming
It inspired a film and many imitators

title: Minecraft Is Fully Released
shortDesc: A block-building sandbox becomes the best-selling video game of all time.
fullDesc: Markus Persson released an early version of Minecraft in 2009, and the full game launched on November 18, 2011. It let players build and explore freely, and it became the best-selling video game ever.
realFacts: Microsoft bought Mojang for $2.5 billion in 2014
More than 300 million copies have sold
It is widely used in schools
Players have built huge worlds and even working computers

title: Grand Theft Auto V Breaks Sales Records
shortDesc: A game earns about a billion dollars in three days.
fullDesc: Rockstar Games released Grand Theft Auto V on September 17, 2013. It reported about $800 million in sales on its first day and passed $1 billion within three days, a record for entertainment at the time.
realFacts: It was released again on newer consoles in 2014 and 2022
It has sold well over 200 million copies
GTA Online kept earning for many years
Rockstar spent years on its follow-up

title: Pokémon Go Gets Millions Walking
shortDesc: An augmented reality game sends players out into the real world.
fullDesc: Niantic released Pokémon Go in July 2016. The phone game placed Pokémon on real maps, and hundreds of millions of people downloaded it within its first year.
realFacts: It had one of the fastest mobile launches ever
Players gathered in parks and landmarks
It boosted interest in augmented reality
Safety concerns arose over distracted players

title: Fortnite Battle Royale Takes Off
shortDesc: A free battle royale mode turns Epic's game into a cultural phenomenon.
fullDesc: Epic Games launched Fortnite Battle Royale as a free mode in September 2017. It grew to hundreds of millions of players and hosted live in-game concerts, including one by Travis Scott in 2020.
realFacts: Epic Games turned it into a huge business
Travis Scott's 2020 concert drew over 12 million live players
Epic sued Apple in 2020 over app store fees
It popularised the battle royale genre

title: Breath of the Wild Launches with the Switch
shortDesc: Nintendo's open-world Zelda becomes one of the most praised games ever.
fullDesc: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild released on March 3, 2017 alongside the Nintendo Switch. Its free-form open world and physics-based play earned widespread critical praise.
realFacts: It helped the Switch become a huge success
It won many Game of the Year awards
Tears of the Kingdom followed in 2023
Developers cite it as an influence on open-world design
wiki: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

title: Elden Ring Is Released
shortDesc: FromSoftware's open-world epic wins Game of the Year.
fullDesc: FromSoftware released Elden Ring on February 25, 2022. The open-world game, with world-building by author George R. R. Martin, sold millions within weeks and won Game of the Year at The Game Awards.
realFacts: It sold 12 million copies in its first month
Hidetaka Miyazaki directed it
A major expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree, released in 2024
Its difficulty sparked wide debate about game design

title: Alan Turing Asks Whether Machines Can Think
shortDesc: A famous paper proposes the imitation game, later called the Turing test.
fullDesc: In October 1950 Alan Turing published Computing Machinery and Intelligence in the journal Mind. He proposed judging machine intelligence by whether a person could tell it apart from a human in conversation.
realFacts: The test became a landmark idea in AI
Turing died in 1954
Modern chatbots are often compared to his test
Debate continues over whether it measures real intelligence

title: The Term Artificial Intelligence Is Born
shortDesc: A summer workshop at Dartmouth founds AI as a field.
fullDesc: In the summer of 1956 John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Claude Shannon and Nathaniel Rochester organised a workshop at Dartmouth College. McCarthy had coined the term artificial intelligence in the proposal, and the meeting is seen as the start of the field.
realFacts: The proposal was written in 1955
It gathered researchers in computing and logic
Early optimism predicted fast progress
AI went through several funding booms and winters afterwards

title: ImageNet Is Presented
shortDesc: A giant labelled photo dataset sets the stage for the deep learning boom.
fullDesc: In 2009 Fei-Fei Li and colleagues presented ImageNet, a dataset of millions of labelled images. An annual contest built on it drove the progress that led to modern image recognition.
realFacts: It grew to more than 14 million images
The yearly contest began in 2010
AlexNet won it in 2012 using deep learning
It showed how much data matters for AI

title: Deep Blue Beats Kasparov
shortDesc: An IBM computer defeats the world chess champion in a match.
fullDesc: In May 1997 IBM's Deep Blue beat world champion Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5 in a six-game match in New York. It was the first time a reigning champion lost a match to a computer under standard conditions.
realFacts: Kasparov had beaten an earlier version in 1996
Kasparov accused IBM of cheating
IBM dismantled Deep Blue after the match
Today's phone chess programs are stronger

title: Watson Wins at Jeopardy!
shortDesc: An IBM computer beats the show's greatest champions.
fullDesc: In February 2011 IBM's Watson defeated Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on the quiz show Jeopardy!. It answered questions posed in natural language and won the million-dollar prize.
realFacts: IBM donated the winnings to charity
Watson was later aimed at medicine and business
Those uses had mixed success
It showed the progress of language understanding

title: AlphaGo Beats Lee Sedol
shortDesc: A computer masters the ancient game of Go, long thought out of reach.
fullDesc: In March 2016 Google DeepMind's AlphaGo defeated Go champion Lee Sedol four games to one in Seoul. Go has far more possible positions than chess, and many experts had expected machines to need another decade.
realFacts: Its move 37 in game two stunned experts
Lee Sedol won one game
Lee retired in 2019 citing AI's strength
Later versions learned without human games

title: Attention Is All You Need
shortDesc: Google researchers publish the Transformer design behind modern AI.
fullDesc: In June 2017 researchers at Google published Attention Is All You Need, introducing the Transformer neural network design. It became the foundation of models like BERT and GPT.
realFacts: It replaced older sequence models for language
BERT and GPT were built on it
It scales well with more data and computing power
It underlies today's chatbots and image models

title: OpenAI Unveils GPT-3
shortDesc: A language model with 175 billion parameters writes surprisingly human text.
fullDesc: In May 2020 OpenAI described GPT-3, a language model with 175 billion parameters. It could write essays, code and stories from short prompts, and it showed what scaling up could do.
realFacts: It was made available through an API in June 2020
It was far larger than earlier models
Its text sometimes contained confident errors
It paved the way for ChatGPT in 2022

title: AlphaFold Solves Protein Folding
shortDesc: DeepMind's AI predicts protein structures with near-lab accuracy.
fullDesc: In late 2020 DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 won the CASP14 contest by predicting protein shapes with near laboratory accuracy. It has been called a solution to a 50-year biology problem.
realFacts: DeepMind released predicted structures for about 200 million proteins in 2022
The database is free for scientists
Demis Hassabis and John Jumper shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry
It speeds up drug and biology research

title: Stable Diffusion Goes Open Source
shortDesc: An open image generator puts text-to-picture AI in everyone's hands.
fullDesc: In August 2022 Stability AI released Stable Diffusion, an image generator whose code and weights were public. Unlike closed tools, anyone could run and change it, which fuelled a wave of AI art and lawsuits over training data.
realFacts: DALL-E 2 and Midjourney arrived the same year
Artists sued over training data
Open models spread quickly
It set off a debate about copyright and creativity

title: GPT-4 Is Released
shortDesc: OpenAI's model passes professional exams and accepts images.
fullDesc: OpenAI released GPT-4 on March 14, 2023. It could take images as well as text and scored high on many professional and academic tests, extending the surge that began with ChatGPT.
realFacts: It powered a paid tier of ChatGPT
Microsoft built it into Bing
Rivals like Claude and Gemini followed
It renewed debate about AI safety and jobs

title: AI Wins Nobel Prizes
shortDesc: The Physics and Chemistry Nobels both honour artificial intelligence work.
fullDesc: In October 2024 the Nobel Prize in Physics went to John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton for foundations of neural networks. The Chemistry prize went to Demis Hassabis and John Jumper for protein structure prediction, shared with David Baker.
realFacts: Hinton had left Google in 2023 to speak about AI risks
Hassabis led DeepMind
Baker was honoured for computational protein design
It marked AI's arrival in mainstream science

title: The Great Fire of London
shortDesc: A bakery blaze burns most of the medieval city.
fullDesc: The Great Fire began in a bakery on Pudding Lane on September 2, 1666 and burned for four days. It destroyed about 13,200 houses and 87 churches, including old St Paul's Cathedral.
realFacts: Few deaths were officially recorded
Christopher Wren designed many new churches
New building rules required brick and stone
A monument to the fire stands near its origin

title: The Hindenburg Disaster
shortDesc: A hydrogen airship bursts into flames as it lands, ending the airship age.
fullDesc: On May 6, 1937 the German airship Hindenburg caught fire while landing at Lakehurst, New Jersey. Thirty-six people died, and filmed footage and radio coverage shocked the world.
realFacts: It was filled with flammable hydrogen
Newsreel footage and a radio broadcast spread the news
Passenger airship travel ended soon after
The exact cause is still debated

title: Three Mile Island Accident
shortDesc: A partial meltdown in Pennsylvania shakes public trust in nuclear power.
fullDesc: On March 28, 1979 a reactor at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania suffered a partial meltdown after equipment failures and operator mistakes. Little radiation escaped, but the accident shaped nuclear policy in the United States.
realFacts: No deaths were directly linked to the accident
It led to stricter safety rules
New US reactor orders slowed sharply
Unit 2 never reopened
wiki: Three Mile Island Nuclear Generating Station

title: The Bhopal Gas Tragedy
shortDesc: A chemical leak in India kills thousands in the worst industrial disaster ever.
fullDesc: On the night of December 2 to 3, 1984 a toxic gas leaked from a Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India. Thousands died soon afterwards and many more suffered lasting harm.
realFacts: Estimates of deaths range from thousands to far higher
The gas was methyl isocyanate
Union Carbide paid a settlement in 1989
Cleanup and compensation disputes have lasted decades

title: The Challenger Disaster
shortDesc: The space shuttle breaks apart 73 seconds after launch.
fullDesc: On January 28, 1986 the space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff, killing all seven crew members, including teacher Christa McAuliffe. A failed rubber seal in the cold weather was the cause.
realFacts: The Rogers Commission investigated, including Richard Feynman
Shuttle flights paused for 32 months
NASA's decision-making was criticised
It became a case study in engineering ethics

title: The Columbia Disaster
shortDesc: The shuttle Columbia breaks up while returning to Earth.
fullDesc: On February 1, 2003 the space shuttle Columbia disintegrated as it re-entered the atmosphere, killing all seven astronauts. A piece of foam had damaged its wing during launch.
realFacts: The investigation blamed both the foam strike and NASA's culture
Shuttle flights paused for over two years
NASA retired the shuttle fleet in 2011
The crew included Kalpana Chawla and Ilan Ramon

title: The Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill
shortDesc: A rig explosion causes the largest marine oil spill in history.
fullDesc: On April 20, 2010 an explosion on the Deepwater Horizon drilling rig killed 11 workers and began a leak that spilled about 4.9 million barrels of oil into the Gulf of Mexico over 87 days.
realFacts: BP agreed to billions in fines and settlements
The spill harmed wildlife and coastal industries
The well was sealed in September 2010
New offshore safety rules followed

title: The Boeing 737 MAX Crashes
shortDesc: Two crashes kill 346 people and ground a whole airliner for nearly two years.
fullDesc: A Lion Air 737 MAX crashed in October 2018 and an Ethiopian Airlines one in March 2019, killing 346 people in total. A flight control system called MCAS was involved, and the plane was grounded worldwide for about 20 months.
realFacts: Regulators faced questions over how the plane was certified
Boeing's chief executive resigned in 2019
The plane returned to service in late 2020
Boeing faced further scrutiny over quality in later years

title: The Ever Given Blocks the Suez Canal
shortDesc: One giant container ship stops about 12 percent of world trade.
fullDesc: On March 23, 2021 the container ship Ever Given ran aground and blocked the Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships waited, and the jam showed how fragile global shipping can be.
realFacts: About 12 percent of world trade passes through the canal
Tugboats and dredgers freed the ship on March 29
Costs ran into billions of dollars per day of delay
The owners and canal authority settled in 2021

title: The Titan Submersible Implodes
shortDesc: A tourist submersible is lost on a dive to the Titanic wreck.
fullDesc: On June 18, 2023 the OceanGate submersible Titan lost contact on a dive to the Titanic wreck. Debris was found days later, and all five people on board were killed by an implosion.
realFacts: OceanGate's founder Stockton Rush was among the dead
Experts had warned about its experimental carbon fibre hull
A US Coast Guard inquiry followed
OceanGate suspended operations

title: The CrowdStrike Outage
shortDesc: A faulty software update crashes millions of computers worldwide.
fullDesc: On July 19, 2024 a faulty update from the security firm CrowdStrike crashed about 8.5 million Windows computers. Airlines, hospitals and banks were disrupted around the world.
realFacts: Thousands of flights were cancelled
The fix needed manual repair on many machines
CrowdStrike explained the cause in a report
It showed risks of relying on a few software vendors

title: The Y2K Bug Arrives
shortDesc: The world fixes its computers and midnight passes with few problems.
fullDesc: Many computer systems stored years with two digits, so the change from 1999 to 2000 was feared to cause failures. Governments and companies spent huge sums on fixes, and January 1, 2000 passed with only minor issues.
realFacts: Global spending on fixes is estimated in the hundreds of billions of dollars
Disaster predictions did not come true
Experts still argue about whether the fear was overblown
It boosted work on legacy software
